title: Ai assisted qte video game idea
author: intellectualsayian7
selftext: I was thinking of a video game that I wanted to make where it one of those qte games that where the players make the decisions but using ai to give you limitless response choices and the characters/ai reaction can adapt to any response you give depending on the characterization of the characters. Could this be controversial?

comments.author: JamesAlphaWolf
comments.body: Unfortunately, anything that makes use of AI in any way is controversial.

comments.author: Shaz_berries
comments.body: There's just literally no meat to this idea... It's like saying. "What about a game where you are first person and you move around". And???

replies.author: intellectualsayian7
replies.body:
Your right I forgot to add more. Each choice the player makes actually has consequences for example  Cyberpunk 2077 has multiple endings, many dialogue choices throughout the main game have a limited impact on the core storyline and often lead back to the same general outcomes. 

Another example is with Life Is Strange where Decisions primarily affect character relationships and minor events, but major plot elements are often unavoidable and the narrative follows a largely linear path. 

Using Ai to make it possible to generate infinite amount of decision outcomes and possibilities, how every npc will act depending on the npc's characteristics/ personality or even what they are involved in for example: if you were to shoot at a gang affiliated npc either they'll shoot at you or get gang members to come after you later in the game.  Any concerns or ideas.

replies.author: Shaz_berries
replies.body: The problem is your ideas are sooo general. If you actually made a game with AI and let it be "open ended", how can you guarantee any quality control for the players?

replies.author: intellectualsayian7
replies.body: I didn't think of that, but how could we establish control or regulation in the Ai without it being opened ended and give an illusion of infinite dialogue choices the player can make of their character.

replies.author: Shaz_berries
replies.body: Exactly why this idea has little merit IMO. You're describing tools and concepts but not a concrete idea or plan

replies.author: intellectualsayian7
replies.body: Ok, your saying this isn't an idea but more like a concept of using ai in a video game

replies.author: NobodyFlowers
replies.body:
Brother, if you're serious about wanting to make a game like this, dm me. Every creation starts as a concept or idea. You having this thought and being bombarded with people telling you there's nothing novel or no way to make it happen is how ideas die. There is a solid plan to make this happen, but the people with the idea have to come together to make it happen.

I have the blueprint and can explain it in detail. I don't have the resources. If you're serious, let's talk. If not, you'll keep getting the responses like those before.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
Literally every gamedevs first AI idea is "what if it includes ChatGPT that just makes up the game as you go" for infinite worlds, infinite gameplay, etc.

If you've ever talked to ChatGPT for more than ten prompts, you know it loses track of the conversation eventually. All these "consequences" add up and create a massive memory issue over time.

comments.author: LopsidedLobster2100
comments.body: Kinda sounds like going outside and talking to someone

comments.author: Own-Detective-A
comments.body: Have you looked into game dev at all? Or any technical project?

replies.author: intellectualsayian7
replies.body: No, I'm pretty new to it.

replies.body: You have a lot to learn. AI Will only get you a certain way.
